[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was born about 1756. His exact birthplace has not been proved. The estimate comes from his Gilders Creek gravestone, which records that he died on 11 December 1826 aged 70.<ref name="Gilders">[https://genealogytrails.com/scar/newberry/gilders_creek_cem.htm "Gilders Creek Cemetery"], Newberry County, South Carolina, transcription for John Glasgow (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref>

John was a son of [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]] and [[Crosier-512|Mary Crosier]]. James's will, dated 17 October 1775, gave his “well beloved son, John Glasgow” fifty acres. James also directed Mary, Robert and John to support his younger children from the profits of the land.<ref name="JamesWill">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124215937id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_JGlasgowWill.html "Will of James Glasgow"], transcription of Newberry Will Book A, p. 194; will dated 17 October 1775 and proved 13 July 1793 (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref>

Mary's will, dated 5 April 1822, independently called John “my son” and entrusted him with the management of her property during her lifetime.<ref name="MaryWill">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101104164512id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_MaryWill.html "Will of Mary Glasgow"], transcription of Newberry Will Book H, pp. 489–490; will dated 5 April 1822 and proved 14 October 1822 (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref>

John headed a three-person household in Newberry District in 1820. Its age distribution is compatible with John, a wife and [[Glasgow-1145|Absolom Glasgow]], but the schedule does not name anyone except the household head.<ref name="Census1820">[https://archive.org/details/populationsc18200120unit/page/n146/mode/1up 1820 United States census], Newberry District, South Carolina, p. 135, John Glasgow household; NARA microfilm publication M33, roll 120 (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref>

John died on 11 December 1826 and was buried at Gilders Creek.<ref name="Gilders" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1144]] is assessed at 99% (proved). James’s 1775 Newberry will expressly calls John his well-beloved son and devises him fifty acres. Mary’s 1822 will independently calls John her son, while the Gilders Creek family context identifies the selected John and James household.

Confident99%; retained will transcriptions, with no newly inspected original or new mother assignment.

Next useful test: Use the named will family to test less-secure descendants.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124215937id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_JGlasgowWill.html "Will of James Glasgow" (https://web.archive.org/web/20101124215937 id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_JGlasgowWill.html), transcription of Newberry Will Book A, p. 194; will dated 17 October 1775 and proved 13 July 1793 (accessed 12 August 2026).]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20101104164512id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_MaryWill.html "Will of Mary Glasgow" (https://web.archive.org/web/20101104164512 id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_MaryWill.html), transcription of Newberry Will Book H, pp. 489–490; will dated 5 April 1822 and proved 14 October 1822 (accessed 12 August 2026).]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


No inspected record names John's wife.

[[Glasgow-1145|Absolom Glasgow]], born about 1799, is attached as John's son. The 1820 household is compatible with John, a wife and Absolom, but it does not name the younger people and therefore does not itself prove the relationship. No additional son of John has been identified.

Hiram Glasgow should not be added as another son. The will of Mary, widow of [[Glasgow-1982|Wilson Glasgow]], directly calls Hiram her son.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124215757id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_WilsonGlasgowWife.html "Will of Mary, wife of Wilson Glasgow"], transcription of Newberry Will Book N, p. 1; will dated 28 November 1837 and proved 22 October 1838 (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref>

Hiram administered Absolom's estate in 1834 and became guardian of “J L & others” in 1837.<ref>[https://genealogytrails.com/scar/newberry/estates1785-1949/22.htm "Probate court general index to estates, 1785–1949"], entries for Absolom Glasgow, estate 1069, and J. L. Glasgow and others, estate 1901 (accessed 12 August 2026).</ref> These fiduciary roles show a close family connection but do not make Hiram John's son.

[[Glasgow-1146|John Glasgow]] represents the same man. That profile repeats the approximate 1756 birth, exact 11 December 1826 death and Newberry identity, and cites the Gilders Creek memorial for this John. It has no attached relatives that belong to a separate family.

A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glascow, London chairman. John Glascow, a chairman, said he saw a man in black running with pistols after Martha Ray was shot in Covent Garden.<ref>Derby Mercury, provider-labelled 19 March 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394231375/ record]; Old Bailey original, printed p.207; [https://www.dhi.ac.uk/san/ob/1770s/177904040005.gif record]; Old Bailey Proceedings, James Hackman record t17790404-3; event dating only; [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17790404-3 record].</ref> The Old Bailey indictment specifies that Martha Ray was shot on 7 April 1779 (printed p.207); that is the event date, not the indictment or newspaper publication date. The newspaper describes evidence after the shooting, not established trial testimony. Its March provider label is incorrect. The identification remains uncertain.
